sentences.text: Woodbinesuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
Its lower jaw was elongate and slender, fused from the tip to the sixteenth teeth, and lacked a mandibular fenestra.
The holotype, SMU 74626, was found near the base of the formation in Tarrant County by Johnny Allen Byers and J. Maurice in May 1990.
Yuong-Nam Lee tentatively assigned Woodbinesuchus to the family Goniopholidae, though the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group as Pholidosauridae.
This animal lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
Crocodyliform fossils are widespread in the Woodbine Formation where Woodbinesuchus was found.
